newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end sharply lower on rate, property woes.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end sharply lower on rate, property woes.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks tumbled to a sharply lower close on Thursday, rocked by concerns about higher interest rates, government measures to stamp out property speculation and a selloff in Japanese shares.
The Hang Seng Index slid 256.82 points, or 1.91 percent, to close at 13,198.11. Turnover was HK$11.41 billion compared with HK$11.37 billion on Wednesday.

"The index has been under pressure because of worries of an interest rate rise in the U.S. People are also worried about the government taking measures against speculation in the property market," said Dharmala Securities technical analyst Alex Wong.

The yield on the U.S. long bond continued to climb on Wednesday with the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond falling 20/32 to yield 6.84 percent. Analysts said investors were taking cover ahead of the release of U.S. December producer price data on Thursday and the U.S. December jobs report on Friday.
Interest rate sensitive property stocks felt the brunt of the selling, with speculation that the government may step in to dampen escalating property prices adding to the sector's woes.
"The focus of the selling is without doubt on the property sector," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
"There are worries about a property speculation clampdown. That would cap the prices," he added.

Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten said on Wednesday the government was keeping the property market "under urgent review". Shares in Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$3.00 to HK$92.25 and Henderson Land slumped HK$3.00 to HK$73.00.
Cheung Kong, which notched up heavy gains this week on news of a group reorganisation, tumbled HK$2.50 to HK$72.25.
"The market is actually making use of all sorts of excuses to go for an expected consolidation," said Amy Wong, research director at New China Hong Kong Securities.
"One of the excuses they use is actually that the Japanese market is down further today and this has affected sentiment in Hong Kong," she said.
The Nikkei 225 average fell more than three percent on Thursday to its lowest close in more than a year, down 606.51 points at 18,073.87.
Analysts said the Hang Seng Index could see further downside in the short term.
"It may marginally blip below 13,000 but is likely to find major support at 12,800," said Wong.
